anomalies.observed: The positive pin of the BAT connector (J1 pin 1) and the positive pin of the 5V_POWER connector (J8 pin 1) are drawn into the same node/net NET0041. That same node also feeds the anode of D3 (SS54) and the source side of the battery P-FET Q2 (IRLML6402).
anomalies.expected: The specification defines two separate supply paths: the battery input is gated through the P-FET to the /BAT bus net, while the external 5V input is isolated from the board +5V rail by the SS54 series diode. The external 5V jack and the battery connector should not be merged on the same net.

evidence.quote: J8 5V_POWER pin 1 and J1 BAT pin 1 are connected together to the same green node that also connects to D3 SS54 and Q2 IRLML6402; net label NET0041 appears on that node.
J5 | Conn_01x02, labelled BAT | Battery input connector, gated through Q1 to the /BAT bus net.
J7 (labelled 5V_POWER) feeds the board's +5V rail through D1 (SS54 Schottky), which blocks current from flowing back out of the external-power jack.

anomalies.impact: External 5V can appear on the battery node and, when the optional power switch turns Q2 on, be applied to the M5Stack BAT pin. Conversely, battery voltage can back-feed into the external 5V jack. This creates an unintended power path and can damage the M5Stack Core or the external supply.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to merge the battery input and external 5V input on NET0041, contrary to the specification's two separate, diode-isolated power paths.
